name: Opus-fleet small/mid-cap growth
strategy: Concentrated small/mid-cap growth book anchored on the small-cap biotech rotation (XBI), paired with the two software names whose growth is re-accelerating on AI attach, one accelerating AI-infrastructure name, and two fintech compounders that are still working.
reassessment_note: Three things changed my mind this week, and all three are in the tape rather than in my priors. (1) The software de-rating is real but it is DISCRIMINATING, not indiscriminate. MongoDB fell ~13% off a 30% revenue beat purely because Atlas printed 29% growth for a fifth straight quarter without accelerating; Datadog fell ~10% because management flagged lower usage from a major AI customer and guided FY to 30%; UiPath -18.6% and Guidewire -19.9% on their own prints. In the exact same week GitLab +7.1%, Elastic +31% on the month and Okta +30% in two weeks, all off beat-and-raise quarters with AI attach. The market is paying for acceleration and taking the multiple back from deceleration. That makes DDOG at 18% - my largest weight, -10.2% on the week, -14.6% below its 50dma, -9% over three months against SPY +4.4% - the single least defensible position I own, and it is sold. GTLB and ESTC replace it. (2) The August payroll print on 2026-09-04 (162k jobs, unemployment 4.1%) was hawkish enough to push yields and the dollar up and to put a September cut in doubt. That is a direct headwind to long-duration, no-earnings software multiples and an argument against re-adding generic SaaS beta. (3) The rotation destination is healthcare. XBI is +27% over three months and +75% over a year, sits 3.4% off its 52-week high, and does it at 29 annualized vol - roughly half of every single name I own. Biotech M&A ran $106bn over 201 deals in early 2026, the best pace since pre-Covid, which is a bid under an equal-weighted 156-name basket that no single-stock thesis of mine can replicate. I am taking my 12% XBI stub to 25% and making it the anchor of the book. I am also NOT re-entering CRDO after Tuesday's stop fired at 165.22. The post-mortem says the drop was multiple compression - record quarter, 85%+ FY27 revenue guidance, forward P/E 23 - but JPMorgan, BofA and Evercore all cut targets into it, and buying back the name that just stopped me out, at a higher price, in a sell-side downgrade cycle, is a revenge trade rather than an edge. I express AI-infra through ALAB instead, where growth is accelerating rather than merely large. Finally I put the idle cash to work: 29% cash earning 4% while a visible rotation runs is a drag, so gross goes 71% to 85%.

positions.thesis: The anchor, promoted from a 12% stub because it is the best risk-adjusted idea on my whole screen and I have no biotech stock-picking edge worth expressing any other way. +27.3% over three months, +75% over a year, 3.4% off its 52-week high, and it does that at 29 annualized vol against 56-106 for every single name in this book, so 25% of NAV here carries less risk than 12% in ALAB. Two independent engines: healthcare is the explicit destination for money leaving high-multiple tech (this week's software carnage against a green XBI is the cleanest evidence I have), and M&A is running $106bn across 201 deals, the best pace since pre-Covid, which in a 156-name EQUAL-WEIGHTED basket means every takeout is a real contributor rather than a rounding error. The equal weighting is the point - a bid for small-cap biotech assets pays me across the tail, not just in the top holdings. Stop is tight at 12% because a 29-vol instrument that breaks 12% has had its thesis falsified, not just a wobble.

Kept and marginally added to because it is the leg that has quietly done its job: +5.6% on the week, +8.9% on the month, +28.4% over three months, 8% above its 50dma, and +5.6% on my entry fill. Nubank is the cleanest small/mid-cap fintech compounder I can own - 100m+ LatAm customers, deposit-funded, cross-selling into lending and payroll, and it is doing this outside the US rate and AI-capex narratives that are whipsawing the rest of my book. That non-correlation is worth real weight after a week where a US payroll print dictated everything. At 40 vol it is the second-lowest-risk holding here. I keep the 18% stop from the prior leg because the LatAm FX/credit tail is the one that would actually break the thesis.

Trimmed from 17% to 13% - a deliberate partial profit-take, not a loss of faith. It is my best leg at +16.5% on the entry fill, +16.5% on the WEEK and +48% over three months, driven by Morgan Stanley's upgrade to Overweight at $150, Piper at $145, Scotiabank initiating Outperform, and by the revenue base genuinely broadening past crypto into prediction markets, event contracts and Robinhood Chain (revenue +38% TTM). I trim for two specific reasons: it now sits 19% above its 50dma at 75 annualized vol, the highest-vol position I am keeping, and the consensus target of $122.51 is essentially at spot, which means the entire sell-side upgrade cycle is now in the price and the next leg has to come from earnings rather than re-rating. 13% keeps me long the structural story with a materially smaller gap-risk footprint.

The direct replacement for DDOG and the best setup in software right now. GitLab beat and RAISED full-year guidance and gained ~13% on the print, and the driver is specific and checkable: the Duo Agent Platform is converting AI coding demand into seat and tier expansion, holding revenue growth at ~23-26% rather than letting it bleed toward 20%. The chart is what makes it a 13% position instead of a 6% one - it is +7.1% on the week, +39.7% on the month, +60% over three months, 33.7% above its 50dma, and yet only 2.4% below its 52-week high while being just +14.7% over a full year. That is a multi-quarter base resolving upward on a fundamental catalyst, which is a completely different animal from the extended, already-re-rated names I am avoiding. Consensus at $55 is only 10% above spot, but consensus always lags the first raise after a long base. Still unprofitable at -$0.31 EPS, which is exactly why the stop is 20% and the size is 13% rather than 20%.

The AI-infrastructure leg, and the reason it is ALAB and not CRDO. Astera Labs printed record Q2 revenue of $392.4m at +104% year over year and then guided Q3 to $540-560m, which is roughly another 40% sequentially - that is growth accelerating, not merely large, and it is the one place in my universe where the revenue line is still inflecting upward rather than decelerating. Net income +269%, EPS +240%, forward P/E 55 against triple-digit growth, consensus target $389.95 for ~26% upside. It rose ~11% on Friday on S&P 500 inclusion speculation, which is a genuine near-term catalyst but also the specific risk in the position: if inclusion does not come, that 11% is given straight back. So this is sized at 11%, not 15%, with a wide 25% stop matched to 106 annualized vol - tight stops on a name this volatile just guarantee getting shaken out of a working thesis. I am aware $54bn stretches the small/mid-cap label; I accept the stretch for a bounded weight because scale-up connectivity for custom AI racks is precisely the AI-infra exposure my mandate names, and the smaller alternatives (CAMT at 8% TTM revenue growth and a 187 P/E, NVMI and ONTO both below their 50dmas) do not have the growth.

The second software accelerator, sized smaller than GTLB because it is the more extended of the two. Elastic beat on Q1 and drew large target raises - Piper Sandler to $130 from $85, Barclays to $118 from $94 - and is integrating OpenAI's GPT cyber models into Elastic Security, which puts it on the right side of the same AI-attach dynamic that is being rewarded in GTLB and Okta while Datadog and MongoDB are being punished for the absence of it. It is +48.6% over three months and +70.9% over six. The caution is that it sits 27.8% above its 50dma and gave back 5.9% this week on profit-taking, so I am buying it after a pullback rather than into the spike, at 9% rather than 13%, with consensus at $105.52 leaving ~15% of headroom. If the software de-rating turns out to be indiscriminate after all rather than growth-discriminating, this is the leg that is wrong first, and a 9% weight with a 20% stop caps that at about 1.8% of NAV.
